title: American Art
description: From frontier light to mid-century city scenes — the American eye.
source: Art Institute of Chicago, Wikimedia Commons

items.title: The Herring Net
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer's 'The Herring Net' depicts two fishermen hauling in a net teeming with fish, their small dory battling the choppy waters of the open sea. The dynamic composition and raw portrayal capture the arduous labor and natural forces faced by those working the maritime environment.
items.tags: maritime, realism, american art, fishing, labor, ocean, 19th century

items.title: After the Hurricane, Bahamas
items.medium: Transparent watercolor, with touches of opaque watercolor, rewetting, blotting and scraping, over graphite, on moderately thick, moderately textured (twill texture on verso), ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer masterfully captures the raw aftermath of a devastating storm in the Bahamas, depicting a lone figure surveying the wreckage on a desolate shore. Executed primarily in transparent watercolor, the work showcases Homer's skill in rendering light, atmosphere, and the enduring power of nature.
items.tags: hurricane, bahamas, seascape, aftermath, watercolor, realism, solitude, 19th century

items.title: Croquet Scene
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer's 'Croquet Scene' captures a moment of leisure in 19th-century America, depicting figures engaged in the popular lawn game. Painted in 1866, this oil on canvas work reflects the changing social customs and outdoor pursuits of the post-Civil War era.
items.tags: croquet, leisure, social scene, 19th century, American art, genre painting, Winslow Homer, realism

items.title: The Water Fan
items.medium: Watercolor, with blotting and touches of scraping, over graphite, on thick, rough twill-textured, ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer's 'The Water Fan' captures the dynamic interplay of light and water with remarkable immediacy, utilizing the unique properties of watercolor. This evocative work demonstrates Homer's mastery in depicting the power and subtle beauty of the natural world.
items.tags: watercolor, seascape, ocean, nature, American art, late 19th century, realism

items.title: Life-Size Black Bass
items.medium: Transparent watercolor, with touches of opaque watercolor, rewetting, blotting and scraping, over graphite, on thick, moderately textured (twill texture on verso), ivory wove paper (left, right and lower edges trimmed)
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer's 'Life-Size Black Bass' vividly portrays the aquatic subject using transparent watercolor. Created in 1904, this artwork showcases the artist's distinctive ability to capture nature with striking immediacy.
items.tags: fish, bass, wildlife, watercolor, realism, nature, american art

items.title: Stowing Sail
items.medium: Transparent watercolor, with touches of opaque watercolor, rewetting, blotting, scraping and graphite, on thick, moderately textured (twill texture on verso), ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer masterfully captures the dynamic energy of mariners at sea as they prepare a vessel's sails. His command of transparent watercolor is evident in this vivid maritime scene.
items.tags: maritime, sailing, watercolor, american art, sea, labor, early 20th century

items.title: North Woods Club, Adirondacks (The Interrupted Tete-a-Tete)
items.medium: Watercolor, with rewetting, blotting and scraping, over graphite, on thick, moderately textured, ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer's 'North Woods Club, Adirondacks' captures a scene from the wilderness, its subtitle suggesting an 'interrupted tête-à-tête' within nature. Created in watercolor with techniques like rewetting and scraping, the work demonstrates Homer's skill in depicting the rugged beauty of the Adirondacks.
items.tags: adirondacks, nature, wilderness, watercolor, american art, 19th century, realism

items.title: Mount Washington
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer's "Mount Washington" captures the majestic presence of New Hampshire's highest peak. This painting exemplifies Homer's keen observation of the American landscape and its natural grandeur.
items.tags: mountain, landscape, nature, american art, realism, grandeur, new england

items.title: Peach Blossoms
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas painting, titled "Peach Blossoms," was created by American artist Winslow Homer in 1878. It depicts the delicate beauty of peach blossoms, a common subject in nature-focused art.
items.tags: landscape, nature, american art, 19th century, realism, painting

items.title: Coast of Maine
items.description_narrative: This powerful oil painting by Winslow Homer captures the rugged grandeur of the Maine coastline, a frequent subject for the artist in his later career. Depicting turbulent waters crashing against stark rock formations, it embodies his masterful portrayal of nature's raw power and isolation.
items.tags: maine, coastline, ocean, realism, american art, landscape, marine art, nature

items.title: The Rapids, Hudson River, Adirondacks
items.medium: Transparent watercolor, with traces of opaque watercolor, blotting, and scraping, over graphite, on thick, rough-textured, ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer masterfully captures the dynamic power of nature in 'The Rapids, Hudson River, Adirondacks,' showcasing rushing water and rugged terrain. Executed in transparent watercolor, with subtle touches of opaque watercolor and scraping, the work demonstrates Homer's profound connection to the American wilderness.
items.tags: watercolor, landscape, american art, nature, realism, hudson river, adirondacks

items.title: Fishing off Scarborough
items.medium: Graphite and opaque white watercolor, with traces of black chalk, on medium weight, slightly-textured, tan laid paper with blue and red fibers
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer captures the rugged essence of coastal life in 'Fishing off Scarborough,' depicting maritime activity with a sense of immediate observation. Executed with graphite and opaque white watercolor, this work showcases his mastery in rendering light and atmosphere on paper.
items.tags: fishing, marine, coast, watercolor, drawing, American art, realism

items.title: Adirondacks Guide
items.medium: Transparent watercolor with touches of opaque watercolor, rewetting, blotting and scraping, over traces of graphite, on thick, moderately textured, ivory wove paper (top edge trimmed)
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer's "Adirondacks Guide" from 1892 portrays a solitary figure within the rugged landscape of the Adirondack mountains. This watercolor, created with techniques like rewetting and scraping, showcases Homer's distinctive approach to capturing natural light and atmosphere.
items.tags: adirondacks, guide, nature, watercolor, winslow homer, american art, realism, 19th century

items.title: The Watcher, Tynemouth
items.medium: Transparent and opaque watercolor, with rewetting, blotting, and scraping, heightened with gum glaze, over graphite, on moderately thick, slightly textured, cream wove paper (all edges trimmed)
items.description_narrative: This watercolor depicts a solitary figure intently observing the dramatic coastal environment of Tynemouth. Homer masterfully employed transparent and opaque watercolors, along with techniques like rewetting and scraping, to capture the atmosphere and texture of the scene.
items.tags: seascape, watercolor, realism, coast, figure, observer, Tynemouth

items.title: Boy in Boat, Gloucester
items.medium: Transparent watercolor, with touches of opaque watercolor and scraping, over graphite, on moderately thick, rough-textured, ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer's 'Boy in Boat, Gloucester' depicts a lone figure navigating the waters off Gloucester, Massachusetts. Executed in transparent watercolor with touches of opaque watercolor and scraping, this work showcases Homer's mastery of the medium and his focus on maritime themes.
items.tags: american art, watercolor, maritime, realism, gloucester, boy, boat

items.title: Campfire, Adirondacks
items.medium: Transparent and opaque watercolor, with blotting and scraping, on thick, moderately-textured, ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer's 'Campfire, Adirondacks,' created around 1892, captures a nocturnal scene of figures gathered by firelight in the wilderness. This watercolor work demonstrates his skillful use of transparent and opaque washes, along with blotting and scraping techniques, to render the flickering light and rugged atmosphere.
items.tags: campfire, adirondacks, nature, wilderness, american realism, watercolor, night scene

items.title: The Fountain, Villa Torlonia, Frascati, Italy
items.description_narrative: John Singer Sargent captures the grand fountain at Villa Torlonia in Frascati, Italy. The artwork masterfully renders the play of light and shadow across the water and surrounding classical architecture.
items.tags: landscape, Italy, fountain, villa, oil painting, light, Edwardian, architecture

items.title: Mrs. George Swinton (Elizabeth Ebsworth)
items.description_narrative: John Singer Sargent's 1897 portrait of Mrs. George Swinton captures her elegant pose and sophisticated attire. This oil on canvas exemplifies Sargent's mastery of society portraiture and his distinctive brushwork.
items.tags: portrait, oil painting, society portraiture, gilded age, elegance, late 19th century, realism, london society

items.title: Madame Paul Escudier (Louise Lefevre)
items.description_narrative: John Singer Sargent's oil on canvas portrait of Madame Paul Escudier (Louise Lefevre) captures the sitter with characteristic elegance and directness. Painted in 1882, the work exemplifies Sargent's mastery of light and texture in rendering a commanding social presence.
items.tags: portrait, woman, society portraiture, realism, elegant, 19th century, american art

items.title: Life Study (Study of an Egyptian Girl)
items.description_narrative: John Singer Sargent's 'Life Study (Study of an Egyptian Girl)' captures a moment of quiet observation through the artist's masterful brushwork. Executed in 1891, this oil on canvas work exemplifies Sargent's ability to render the human form with both immediacy and profound dignity.
items.tags: portrait, life study, egyptian, female figure, oil painting, john singer sargent, realism, late 19th century

items.title: Venetian Glass Workers
items.description_narrative: John Singer Sargent captures the intense labor and vibrant atmosphere of a glass-blowing workshop in Venice. The painting showcases the dynamic interplay of light and shadow on the workers and their fiery craft.
items.tags: venetian, glassblowing, workers, genre scene, realism, industrial, light, craftsmanship

items.title: Mrs. Charles Gifford Dyer (Mary Anthony)
items.description_narrative: John Singer Sargent's 1880 oil on canvas portrait depicts Mrs. Charles Gifford Dyer, born Mary Anthony, with characteristic elegance. The artist captures the sitter with a sophisticated pose, showcasing his command of light and texture.
items.tags: portrait, oil painting, American art, female sitter, elegance, realism, society portraiture

items.title: Rehearsal of the Pasdeloup Orchestra at the Cirque d'Hiver
items.description_narrative: John Singer Sargent captures a moment of intense concentration during a rehearsal of the Pasdeloup Orchestra at the Cirque d'Hiver. The oil on canvas medium brings to life the vibrant energy and dynamic atmosphere of the performance space.
items.tags: orchestra, rehearsal, music, parisian life, candid, realism, 19th century

items.title: Mrs. Charles Deering (Marion Denison Whipple)
items.description_narrative: John Singer Sargent masterfully captures the elegant presence of Marion Denison Whipple, Mrs. Charles Deering, in this striking 1888 oil portrait. Through vibrant brushwork and a keen eye for detail, Sargent conveys the sitter's poise and the refined aesthetic of the late 19th century.
items.tags: portrait, oil painting, woman, elegant, realist, late 19th century, american artist, society portrait

items.title: American Gothic
items.description_narrative: A stern-faced farmer standing beside his spinster daughter in front of a house with a distinctive Gothic window. One of the most familiar images in 20th-century American art, it is an ambiguous statement about rural American character.
items.tags: portrait, american, gothic, rural, farmer, pitchfork

items.title: Whistler's Mother
items.description_narrative: Formally titled 'Arrangement in Grey and Black No.1', this austere portrait of Whistler's mother seated in profile has become an American cultural icon and symbol of motherhood. Its restrained palette and compositional harmony exemplify Whistler's belief in art for art's sake.
items.tags: portrait, mother, seated, profile, tonalism, grey

items.title: Nighthawks
items.description_narrative: Four figures sit in a brightly lit diner at night on a desolate city corner. The painting captures the loneliness and alienation of modern urban life with cinematic intensity. It has become one of the most reproduced paintings in American art.
items.tags: diner, night, urban, loneliness, realism, american

items.title: Watson and the Shark
items.description_narrative: Copley's dramatic canvas depicts the real 1749 shark attack on young Brook Watson in Havana harbor, its diagonal composition and multiracial crew capturing Enlightenment-era heroism. It became one of the first American history paintings to gain international acclaim and now anchors the National Gallery of Art's collection.
items.tags: history painting, maritime, drama, colonial america, shark attack, national gallery

items.title: Kindred Spirits
items.description_narrative: Painted as a tribute to the recently deceased Thomas Cole, this idealized Catskills landscape shows Cole and poet William Cullen Bryant conversing on a rocky ledge above a wooded gorge. It became the defining manifesto of the Hudson River School's reverence for the American wilderness.
items.tags: hudson river school, landscape, catskills, friendship, american wilderness, romanticism

items.title: The Gross Clinic
items.description_narrative: Eakins depicts the renowned surgeon Samuel Gross lecturing mid-operation in a Philadelphia amphitheater, rendered with unsparing clinical detail that shocked contemporary audiences. Its raw honesty and Rembrandt-like handling of light now rank it among the greatest American paintings of the 19th century.
items.tags: realism, medicine, surgery, philadelphia, portraiture, 19th century

items.title: Among the Sierra Nevada, California
items.description_narrative: Bierstadt's sweeping, light-flooded vista of jagged peaks, a placid lake, and grazing deer romanticizes the American West as an untouched Eden. Exhibited to great acclaim in the East, it helped shape the era's popular imagination of the western frontier.
items.tags: rocky mountain school, western landscape, sierra nevada, sublime, wilderness, luminism

items.title: Twilight in the Wilderness
items.description_narrative: Painted on the eve of the Civil War, Church's uninhabited wilderness scene blazes with a fiery, crimson-streaked sunset reflected across a still New England river. Devoid of any human figure, it stands as a luminist meditation on nature's sublime, unsettled grandeur.
items.tags: hudson river school, luminism, sunset, wilderness, new england, sublime

items.title: The Veteran in a New Field
items.description_narrative: A discharged Union soldier, his jacket and canteen cast aside, harvests a golden field of wheat with a single-bladed scythe. Painted just after the war's end and Lincoln's assassination, the scythe evokes the Grim Reaper and the vast toll of the fallen.

items.title: The Heart of the Andes
items.description_narrative: A monumental South American panorama distills Church's travels retracing the naturalist Alexander von Humboldt, from snow-capped peaks to tropical foreground foliage. When first shown, paying crowds viewed the canvas through a curtained frame with opera glasses as if peering through a window.

items.title: The Rocky Mountains, Lander's Peak
items.description_narrative: A luminous, idealized vista of the Wind River Range rises above a Shoshone encampment, based on sketches from an 1859 survey expedition. The grand image fed Eastern fascination with the frontier and helped define the mythology of the American West.

items.title: The Boating Party
items.description_narrative: A dark-clad oarsman rows a mother and restless child across sunlit water near Antibes, the composition boldly cropped and tilted upward. Its flattened planes of color reveal Cassatt's deep study of Japanese woodblock prints.

items.title: The Fall of the Cowboy
items.description_narrative: Two cowboys pause at a barbed-wire fence gate in a bleak wintry plain, one dismounted to work the wire. Painted to illustrate a Harper's Monthly article, it is an elegy for the vanishing open range that barbed wire had begun to close.

items.title: Symphony in White, No. 1: The White Girl
items.description_narrative: A full-length portrait of Whistler's model and companion Joanna Hiffernan, dressed in white and standing on a wolfskin before a white curtain. Rejected by the Paris Salon, it caused a sensation at the 1863 Salon des Refuses and became a manifesto of art-for-art's-sake Aestheticism.

items.title: After the Bullfight
items.description_narrative: Painted during a trip to Spain, this work shows Cassatt experimenting with the bold brushwork and dark palette of Spanish masters such as Velázquez before she settled permanently in Paris. It depicts a matador in his traje de luces, a subject that fascinated many foreign artists visiting 19th-century Spain.

items.title: Love of Winter
items.description_narrative: George Bellows painted this vigorous scene of ice skaters in New York's Central Park at the height of his engagement with everyday urban recreation. Its bright winter palette and dynamic composition are characteristic of the Ashcan School's embrace of modern American life as subject matter.

items.title: Icebound
items.description_narrative: John Henry Twachtman's 'Icebound' captures a serene winter landscape, likely reflecting the artist's home in Greenwich, Connecticut. The composition features a muted palette and delicate brushwork, evoking the quiet beauty and reflective atmosphere of a snow-covered scene.
items.tags: winter, landscape, snow, ice, impressionism, american impressionism, serene, subtle

items.title: The Artist in His Studio
items.medium: Oil on paper mounted on panel
items.description_narrative: James McNeill Whistler's 'The Artist in His Studio' offers an intimate glimpse into a painter's private creative space. Rendered in oil on paper mounted on panel, the work subtly reveals details of the artistic environment during the mid-19th century.
items.tags: artist, studio, interior, oil painting, 19th century, american art, british art

items.title: Rip Van Winkle
items.description_narrative: This painting depicts a scene from Washington Irving's classic American short story, 'Rip Van Winkle,' first published in 1819. John Quidor frequently drew inspiration from literary sources, bringing narrative depth to his canvases.
items.tags: american painting, romanticism, literature, folklore, narrative, oil painting

items.title: At Mouquin's
items.description_narrative: William Glackens's 'At Mouquin's' captures a lively restaurant interior, depicting patrons engaged in dining and conversation. Rendered in oil on canvas, this 1905 work exemplifies a candid observation of urban life.
items.tags: restaurant, urban life, genre scene, american art, ashcan school, early 20th century, social realism

items.title: The Advance-Guard, or The Military Sacrifice (The Ambush)
items.description_narrative: Frederic Remington captures a tense moment in *The Advance-Guard*, depicting a military unit on alert, possibly anticipating conflict, amidst a rugged landscape. This oil painting exemplifies Remington's dedication to illustrating the dynamic and often perilous realities of the American West.
items.tags: western art, american west, military, frontier, horses, oil painting, realism, late 19th century

items.title: A Parisian Beggar Girl
items.description_narrative: An early figure study depicting a ragged young girl standing barefoot against a plain ground. Painted in 1877 during Sargent's student years in Paris, it already shows his precocious command of tone and light.
items.tags: beggar girl, figure study, Paris, early work, child, realism, portrait

items.title: Rio dei Mendicanti, Venice
items.description_narrative: A luminous watercolor looking down a quiet Venetian canal lined with weathered facades. Made during Sargent's later Venetian campaigns, it is held at Newfields (Indianapolis Museum of Art).
items.tags: Venice, canal, watercolor, cityscape, Italy, reflections, architecture

items.title: On His Holidays, Norway
items.description_narrative: A large plein-air portrait of a boy stretched out beside a river with his rod and a freshly caught salmon. Painted on a 1901 Norwegian fishing holiday, it is held by the Lady Lever Art Gallery, Port Sunlight.
items.tags: Norway, boy, fishing, salmon, plein air, portrait, landscape

items.title: Under the Willows
items.description_narrative: A shimmering watercolor of figures resting in dappled shade beneath willow branches. Dating from about 1888, it belongs to the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston.
items.tags: willows, watercolor, plein air, dappled light, figures, landscape, leisure

items.title: A Venetian Interior
items.description_narrative: A shadowy genre scene of Venetian women idling and working in a cavernous, dimly lit room. Painted around 1880-1882, it is held by the Carnegie Museum of Art, Pittsburgh.
items.tags: Venice, interior, women, genre scene, atmospheric, early work, Italy

items.title: The Patio
items.description_narrative: A sunlit study of a Spanish courtyard with a figure reclining in the shade. Painted during Sargent's 1908 travels in Spain, it is held by the Cleveland Museum of Art.
items.tags: Spain, patio, courtyard, sunlight, figure, travel, architecture

items.title: Simplon Pass: The Tease
items.description_narrative: An informal alpine sketch of two young women resting outdoors, one playfully teasing the other. Painted around 1911 near the Simplon Pass, it is held by the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
items.tags: Simplon Pass, Alps, women, plein air, informal, Boston, leisure

items.title: The Garden Wall
items.description_narrative: A luminous watercolor of two young women seated against a sunlit garden wall, worked with wax-resist highlights over graphite. Painted in 1910, it is held by the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
items.tags: garden wall, watercolor, women, sunlight, plein air, Boston, informal

items.title: An Artist in His Studio
items.description_narrative: A tightly framed interior showing a fellow painter at work amid the clutter of a cramped mountain-inn room. Painted in 1904, it is held by the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
items.tags: studio, artist, interior, painter, genre scene, Boston, plein air

items.title: Lake O'Hara
items.description_narrative: A brilliant mountain landscape of Lake O'Hara in the Canadian Rockies. Painted during Sargent's 1916 expedition, it is held by the Harvard Art Museums (Fogg Museum).
items.tags: Lake O'Hara, Canadian Rockies, mountains, landscape, wilderness, 1916, Harvard

items.title: Village Children
items.description_narrative: A freely brushed oil study of children gathered together outdoors. Dating from about 1890, it is held by the Yale University Art Gallery.
items.tags: children, village, figures, genre scene, plein air, Yale, informal

items.title: The Interior of a Hospital Tent
items.description_narrative: A wartime watercolor of wounded soldiers resting on cots inside a sunlit hospital tent. Painted in 1918 while Sargent served as an official war artist on the Western Front, it is held by the Imperial War Museum, London.
items.tags: World War I, hospital, soldiers, war art, watercolor, 1918, Imperial War Museum

items.title: A Spanish Madonna
items.description_narrative: An oil study of a Spanish devotional Madonna figure encountered on Sargent's early Spanish travels. Dating from around 1879-1880, it is held by the Saint Louis Art Museum.
items.tags: Spain, Madonna, religious, devotional, sculpture, travel, Saint Louis

items.title: An Out-of-Doors Study
items.description_narrative: An Impressionist plein-air scene of a painter and companion working outdoors in bright sunlight. Painted in 1889, it is held by the Brooklyn Museum.
items.tags: plein air, artist, Impressionism, outdoors, sunlight, figures, painting

items.title: Prince Baltasar Carlos on Horseback (after Velázquez)
items.description_narrative: A vigorous copy Sargent made after Velázquez's equestrian portrait of Prince Baltasar Carlos in the Prado. Painted in 1879, it reflects his lifelong study of the Spanish master.
items.tags: after Velázquez, copy, equestrian, Prado, Spain, prince, study

items.title: I Gesuati (The Church of the Gesuati, Venice)
items.description_narrative: A fluid watercolor of a Venetian canal before the church of the Gesuati on the Giudecca. It dates from Sargent's later Venetian watercolor campaigns of about 1903-1909.
items.tags: Venice, watercolor, canal, church, Gesuati, Italy, architecture

items.title: The Mosquito Net
items.description_narrative: An intimate interior showing a woman reclining and reading beneath a gauzy mosquito net. Painted in 1908, it is held by the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
items.tags: interior, woman, reading, mosquito net, leisure, Boston, intimate

items.title: Landscape with Goats
items.description_narrative: A sunlit landscape with goats grazing among rocks and foliage. Painted in 1909, it is held by the Freer Gallery of Art, Washington.
items.tags: landscape, goats, animals, plein air, sunlight, Freer, pastoral

items.title: Franciscan Monk in the Garden of Gethsemane
items.description_narrative: A study of a robed Franciscan monk standing among the olive trees of a garden. Painted around 1905-1906, it is held by the Portland Art Museum.
items.tags: monk, Franciscan, garden, religious, figure, Portland, olive trees

items.title: Simplon Pass
items.description_narrative: A broadly painted alpine landscape of the Simplon Pass in the Swiss Alps. Dating from about 1911, it is held by the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
items.tags: Simplon Pass, Alps, mountains, landscape, Switzerland, plein air, National Gallery of Art

items.title: Trees
items.description_narrative: A rapid watercolor study of trees and dappled foliage. Dating from about 1913, it typifies Sargent's fluent later landscape sketches.
items.tags: trees, watercolor, foliage, landscape, study, plein air, nature

items.title: Simplon Pass: Mrs Barnard and Her Daughter Dorothy
items.description_narrative: An alpine sketch of two seated figures, members of the Barnard family, resting during a Simplon Pass sojourn. Dating from about 1911, it is held by the Barber Institute of Fine Arts, Birmingham.
items.tags: Simplon Pass, figures, Barnard, Alps, plein air, Barber Institute, leisure

items.title: Angels, Mosaic, Palatine Chapel, Palermo
items.description_narrative: A watercolor and gouache study of the Byzantine angel mosaics in the Cappella Palatina, Palermo, made as Sargent researched his Boston Public Library murals. It dates from about 1897-1903 and is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
items.tags: mosaic, Palermo, Byzantine, angels, watercolor, study, Metropolitan Museum

items.title: Two Figures in a Boat, Isola Bella
items.description_narrative: A plein-air watercolor of two figures in a boat on the water at Isola Bella in the Italian Lakes. Painted in 1902, it is held by the Barber Institute of Fine Arts, Birmingham.
items.tags: Isola Bella, boat, watercolor, Italian lakes, figures, plein air, Barber Institute

items.title: Glacier Streams, The Simplon
items.description_narrative: A shimmering study of meltwater streams among alpine rocks near the Simplon Pass. Dating from about 1910, it is held by the Museum of Fine Arts, Springfield, Massachusetts.
items.tags: Simplon, glacier, streams, Alps, landscape, water, mountains

items.title: A Tarpaulin over a Dug-out, Ransart
items.description_narrative: A wartime watercolor of a tarpaulin stretched over a soldiers' dug-out near Ransart on the Western Front. Painted in 1918 during Sargent's service as a war artist, it is held by the Imperial War Museum, London.
items.tags: World War I, dug-out, trench, war art, watercolor, 1918, Imperial War Museum

items.title: A Street in Arras
items.description_narrative: A wartime watercolor looking down a shattered street in the French town of Arras. Painted in 1918 while Sargent was an official war artist, it is held by the Imperial War Museum, London.
items.tags: World War I, Arras, ruins, street, war art, watercolor, Imperial War Museum

items.title: Ada Rehan
items.description_narrative: A full-length society portrait of the celebrated American actress Ada Rehan in a shimmering gown. Painted around 1894-1895, it is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
items.tags: Ada Rehan, actress, portrait, society, full-length, Metropolitan Museum, Gilded Age

items.title: Boats
items.description_narrative: A quick watercolor study of moored boats and their reflections on the water. Dating from about 1913, it is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
items.tags: boats, watercolor, harbor, reflections, study, Metropolitan Museum, marine

items.title: Alhambra, Granada
items.description_narrative: A watercolor study of sunlit architecture at the Alhambra in Granada, Spain. Painted in 1912, it is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
items.tags: Alhambra, Granada, Spain, watercolor, architecture, Moorish, Metropolitan Museum

items.title: Madonna and Child and Saints (copy after an Italian master)
items.description_narrative: A watercolor copy Sargent made after an Italian Old Master altarpiece of the Madonna and Child with saints. Dating from about 1895-1915, it is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
items.tags: copy, Madonna and Child, Old Master, watercolor, religious, study, Metropolitan Museum

items.title: Two Girls with Parasols at Fladbury
items.description_narrative: A sunlit plein-air scene of two young women shading themselves with parasols beside the river at Fladbury. Painted in 1889, it dates from Sargent's Impressionist summers along the English rivers.
items.tags: parasols, women, plein air, Impressionism, Fladbury, riverside, summer
